# Paths under the clean-room second-review gate (see CLEANROOM.md).
# Prefix match; one entry per line; comments with '#'.
#
# No trailing slash on ANY prefix: a `-sys` binding crate is engine code by any
# reading, and `crates/gwk-pty/` would not have matched `crates/gwk-pty-sys/`.
# The gate should over-cover a sibling, never miss one.
#
# The rule is stated for the crate-family prefixes and holds identically one
# level down. `crates/gwk-tui/src/workspace/` was the one line that violated it,
# and it was the line where it mattered most: multiplexer work split out of
# `workspace/` into a `workspace-adjacent/` or `workspace-detach/` sibling would
# have left the gate matching nothing, with no error and no diff to notice —
# which is the same naming-coin-flip hole as `gwk-host` passing while
# `gwk-pty-host` gates, one directory deeper. The seeded step in the
# `cleanroom-gate` CI job feeds exactly that path and fails if it is not caught.
crates/gwk-pty
# Redundant with the prefix above by construction — `crates/gwk-pty-host`
# already starts with `crates/gwk-pty` — and pre-committed anyway. The header
# comment above named this exact crate as the naming-coin-flip hole before it
# existed; leaving its coverage to the prefix match alone would still be
# correct today and silently wrong the day a sibling crate is named something
# the prefix does not start with. Writing the row is the decision; the prefix
# match is only why the gate does not need it to be first.
crates/gwk-pty-host
crates/gwk-adapter-
crates/gwk-tui/src/workspace
# The production shell adapter owns the shared PTY subscription pump and
# detach/reattach routing. The remaining gridwork CLI stays non-engine.
crates/gridwork/src/tui
# The parity harness, engine-driving half only. Its runners spawn the three
# engine CLIs, drive them, answer their approval asks and kill them; its two
# binaries are the harness entry point and the Claude approval-relay hook the
# runner spawns. That is engine supervision by the category rule's own words,
# and a test harness is not lens code, so the module granularity the rule
# allows is spent keeping the tax off the crate's PURE half rather than off
# this. The crate's own module doc already draws this exact line — "matrix,
# pins and checks are the PURE library ... never a raw wire byte, never a live
# process" — so gating the other half is recording a split that exists, not
# imposing one. The remaining modules carry a not-engine line instead
# (.github/cleanroom-not-engine.txt); a prefix longer than the crate directory
# never classifies the directory itself.
crates/gwk-parity/src/runners
crates/gwk-parity/src/bin
